origin.description: Report whether each string contains a code point from a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, report strings that do not match.

arguments.name: max_count
arguments.text: Stop after this many results of interest. Later elements are NA. Negative means no limit. Zero makes every element NA.

origin.details: The inputs are recycled to the longer length. max_count walks elements in stringi's pattern order, not always from left to right, and counts the result after negate. An empty string follows negate. A missing string or pattern is NA and does not consume max_count.
origin.value: A logical vector. A missing result is NA.
origin.example:
x <- stri_detect_charclass(c("a1", "23"), "\\p{L}")
shown <- paste(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", ifelse(x, "TRUE", "FALSE")), collapse = ", ")
sentence <- paste0('stri_detect_charclass(c("a1", "23"), "\\p{L}") returns ', shown, '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Report whether each string contains a code point from a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, report strings that do not match.

arguments.name: max_count
arguments.text: Stop after this many results of interest. Later elements are NA. Negative means no limit. Zero makes every element NA.

translation.details: The inputs are recycled to the longer length. max_count walks elements in stringi's pattern order, not always from left to right, and counts the result after negate. An empty string follows negate. A missing string or pattern is NA and does not consume max_count.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_detect_charclass
x = stri_detect_charclass(["a1", "23"], "\\p{L}")
shown = ", ".join("NA" if value is None else ("TRUE" if value else "FALSE") for value in x)
sentence = f'stri_detect_charclass(c("a1", "23"), "\\p{{L}}") returns {shown}.'
print(sentence)
